summary: Both prior blocking issues are resolved. No agent-design anti-patterns found in the draft.
analysis: Reviewed the full analysis draft (255 lines) and cross-referenced against the contract JSON. Prior review feedback has been fully addressed: (1) All 5 feedback questions are now registered as feedback-1 with questions Q1-Q5 in the contract (lines 208-243 of contract JSON), matching the prose in the draft (lines 229-239). (2) The misleading registration failure note at line 172 has been replaced with an accurate statement confirming that 6 decisions and 1 feedback item are registered in the contract. Checked all 8 agent-design criteria: No excessive pre-fetching — the draft proposes CLI-based polling via egg-orch, not baking diffs into prompts. No structured output for humans — the hybrid message format (Decision 2) is for inter-agent communication, not human-facing output. No post-processing pipelines — messages route through the orchestrator, agents act directly. No rigid procedures — the draft describes objectives (Phase 1/2/3 incremental approach) rather than micromanaged steps. No prompt-level security — policy enforcement is correctly delegated to the gateway and orchestrator (lines 53, 61). No direct LLM API calls or hardcoded model identifiers (not applicable to an analysis draft). The recommended polling-based approach (Option A) is well-aligned with Claude Code's CLI-tool-based agent model, correctly identified as the best fit given the constraint that agents lack background event loops (line 56). The decision to surface messages via egg-orch CLI rather than SSE or raw API calls is the right agent-mode choice.
suggestions: Feedback question Q2 (agent integration pattern) is the most architecturally significant open question from an agent-mode perspective. When that feedback is resolved, the plan phase should ensure the chosen pattern does not introduce a post-processing pipeline or require injecting large context into prompts. Option (a) — agent periodically calls egg-orch message poll — is the most agent-mode-aligned approach since it lets the agent decide when and how to process messages.
